t:
Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall establish a promotional track system for employees of the Department of Veterans Affairs that the Secretary determines are technical experts pursuant to regulations prescribed by the Secretary for purposes of carrying out this section. Such system shall—
    (1) provide any such employee the opportunity to advance within the Department without being required to transition to a management position; and 
    (2) for purposes of achieving career advancement—
        (A) provide for the establishment of new positions within the Department; and 
        (B) notwithstanding any other provision of law, provide for increases in pay for any such employee.

fable.w: The section contemplates the Secretary prescribing regulations to determine which employees are technical experts, and under the definition a grant or requirement of rulemaking authority counts as participation. The tempting reading is that this is a purely internal personnel matter involving only federal employees, with no outside consultation. That reading fails because the rulemaking itself is the participation mechanism, even though the subject matter is internal.
fable.s: pursuant to regulations prescribed by the Secretary for purposes of carrying out this section

opus.w: The section requires the Secretary to issue regulations deciding which employees count as technical experts. The definition counts required rulemaking as participation, and Example 6 counts regulatory authority even when it is only optional. The tempting 'No' reading treats this as a purely internal personnel matter among federal employees. It is weakened by the rulemaking requirement, although the personnel subject matter, which may be exempt from notice-and-comment, makes this less certain.
opus.s: pursuant to regulations prescribed by the Secretary for purposes of carrying out this section
opus.b: **Step 1: the tempting reading.** This looks like a purely internal personnel matter. It sets up a promotion track for VA employees, and everyone involved is inside the federal government, which would point to "No." But the section also requires the Secretary to identify technical experts "pursuant to regulations prescribed by the Secretary." Under the definition, requiring rulemaking counts as "Yes," and Example 6 treats even optional regulatory authority as participation. One caveat: the Administrative Procedure Act exempts agency personnel matters from notice-and-comment, so this answer is less certain.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a promotional track system for federal employees (technical experts within the Department of Veterans Affairs). Since the individuals involved are federal employees, they are inside the federal government. The definition of participation requires consultation or coordination with people outside the government (e.g., public, states, tribes, private companies). Internal HR policies do not constitute participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall establish a promotional track system for employees of the Department of Veterans Affairs that the Secretary determines are technical experts
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "technical experts" are outside parties whose input is being sought. However, the text explicitly states these are "employees of the Department of Veterans Affairs." Federal employees are inside the federal government. The section describes an internal human resources policy for career advancement, not a process for consulting with the public or other outside entities.
